title: Risk Dashboard: 3 Critical, 2 Elevated, 1 Monitor — The Table Is Set for a Big Move
hook: Hormuz stalemate, MOU fragility, and storage deficit create a binary market. The biggest risk isn't escalation — it's a false sense of security that lures traders into complacent positions before the break.
authorWord: The risk/reward in European gas is terrible for bears and attractive for bulls right now. The asymmetry is clear: downside is capped at ~€35 (full resolution), upside is open at €60-100 (escalation). Why would you sell here?
author: La Rédaction 🦊
details:
🔴 CRITICAL — Hormuz Closure Entering Month 3 (Day 69+): The Strait remains effectively closed with both US and Iranian blockades in place. ~20,000 mariners and 2,000 ships stranded per IMO. ~20% of global LNG supply (70-85 Mt/yr from Qatar, UAE, Oman) is offline. Every additional week of closure adds ~2-3 Mt of lost LNG production and raises the winter supply deficit. Qatar's Ras Laffan restart timeline: end-August at earliest if started in May, per Wood Mackenzie. Two trains permanently damaged. Status: No resolution timeline.

🔴 CRITICAL — MOU Negotiation Fragility: 14-point memorandum under negotiation via Pakistani intermediaries. Trump says he's "not satisfied" with terms (May 8, The Guardian). The April 21-22 brief reopening collapsed within 24 hours — a precedent for rapid reversal. IRGC seized the Epaminondas on April 24 despite ceasefire. UK Parliament notes neither side has removed blockades. US war powers deadline adds time pressure. Status: Fragile, could collapse at any point.

🔴 CRITICAL — EU Storage Deficit: Storage at ~34.3% vs 5-year average significantly higher. Required injection rate: 3,462 GWh/day to hit 90% by Nov 1. Maximum capacity: ~4,200 GWh/day — virtually no margin for disruption. EU Russian LNG spot ban removes ~9 bcm/yr. Hormuz closure removes ~15-20 bcm/yr equivalent. Combined: Europe faces a 25+ bcm/yr supply gap vs normal. Status: Structural, worsening with each week of delayed resolution.

🟡 ELEVATED — Norway Maintenance Season: Summer maintenance at Troll, Kollsnes, and Nyhamna processing plants will reduce Norwegian pipeline exports to Europe by up to a third during scheduled outages. Norway accounts for ~26% of EU gas supply. Any unplanned outage ( Troll has had several in recent years) during maintenance season could spike TTF €3-5/MWh. Status: Seasonal risk, late June-July peak.

🟡 ELEVATED — Super El Niño Probability: NOAA's El Niño Watch: 61% by May-July. ECMWF trending stronger. Potential Super El Niño (Niño 3.4 > +2.0°C) by winter 2026/27. Implications: milder NW European winter (bearish TTF), hotter Mediterranean summer (bullish gas-for-power), disrupted Asian hydro (bullish JKM). Net effect on European gas: ambiguous but increases uncertainty. Status: Building, next NOAA update May 14.

🟢 MONITOR — US LNG Supply Ramp: Golden Pass first cargo shipped. Plaquemines in full operation. Corpus Christi Stage 3 online. EIA expects record US LNG exports in 2026. Incremental capacity: 2-3 Bcf/d in 2026. While positive for global supply, it cannot replace Qatar's 10+ Bcf/d equivalent. Status: Positive but insufficient to close gap.

💡 Trade Ideas

1. Portfolio Hedge — Long TTF Jun €55 Calls + Long TTF Jun €38 Puts (Collar Flip): Instead of hedging a long position, express a view that both tails are underpriced. The €55 call costs ~€0.40 (pays €15+ on escalation), the €38 put costs ~€0.50 (pays €5+ on deal). Total cost ~€0.90. In a range-bound market (€38-55), you lose the premium. But the combined 60% probability of a significant move in either direction makes this positive expected value.

2. Long TTF Q4 '26 / Short TTF Q3 '26 (Autumn Rally): The seasonal transition from injection-heavy Q3 to withdrawal-prep Q4 is where the storage deficit bites. If injection falls behind (likely), the market wakes up in September-October and bids aggressively for Q4 gas. Buy Oct '26, sell Aug '26. Target spread widening from €0-1 to €5-8.

3. Short EUR/USD as Tail Risk Hedge: Gas crisis escalation would weaken the euro (energy import dependency, trade balance deterioration, ECB policy constraints). A EUR/USD short position provides indirect hedging against the bullish gas scenario. Stop if MOU is signed.

⚡ Dissenting View — Lyra 🎭
You paint three CRITICAL risks, but the market has lived with all three for weeks and TTF hasn't moved. Maybe the market is right — maybe these risks are fully priced. The complacency you diagnose might actually be wisdom: traders have learned that the Hormuz situation can persist for months without triggering a price explosion. The risk isn't that traders are too calm — it's that they'll stay calm for too long and then panic all at once. But timing that panic is the hard part.
